reviewer.title: CS0016 Comprehensive Reviewer: Modules 1–4
reviewer.description: A 200-question comprehensive reviewer covering Modules 1–4, with substantial standalone coverage for Modules 1 and 2 and broader coverage of Modules 3 and 4.

questions.question: In virtualization terminology, what is a virtual computer commonly called?
questions.explanation: Virtual machines are often called guests, while physical computers are called hosts.

questions.question: A physical computer that runs virtual machines is commonly called a host.
questions.explanation: The module calls virtual machines guests and physical computers hosts.

questions.question: (Choose 3) Select all objectives included in the Linux Review lab.
questions.explanation: The Linux Review lab includes file management, regular expressions, and system administration.

questions.question: Where are all coding labs in this course performed?
questions.explanation: The module states that all coding labs are performed on a Linux-based VM.

questions.question: Which characteristic of Python is specifically cited as making it easy to obtain, install, and deploy?
choices: It is free, open, and multiplatform
It requires a proprietary operating system
It only runs inside a browser
It eliminates the need for testing
questions.correctAnswer: It is free, open, and multiplatform
questions.explanation: The module describes Python as free, open, and multiplatform.

questions.question: Python provides a solid foundation that can make learning other programming _____ easier and faster.
questions.explanation: The module says Python provides a solid foundation for learning other programming languages.

questions.question: (Choose 3) Select all topics explicitly included in the Python Programming Review lab.
questions.explanation: These three topics are listed as parts of the Python Programming Review lab.

questions.question: Which DevNet feature is a repository of sample code written by other developers?
questions.explanation: Code Exchange is described as a repository of sample code written by other developers.

questions.question: Which DevNet feature provides production-like development and testing environments?
questions.explanation: Sandboxes are described as production-like development and testing environments.

questions.question: (Choose 4) Select all features listed as part of DevNet.
questions.explanation: The module lists Learning Labs, Sandboxes, Code Exchange, developer support, and developer documentation as DevNet features.

questions.question: DevNet provides developers a starting point for Cisco APIs, including API documentation, education, and developer support.
questions.explanation: This is stated in the Getting Started with DevNet Resources section.

questions.question: A pre-configured environment already installed with Cisco platforms is called a DevNet _____.
questions.explanation: The Learning Labs section describes a DevNet Sandbox as a pre-configured environment.

questions.question: Which exchange provides network automation use cases with different solutions and toolkits?
questions.explanation: Automation Exchange provides a collection of network automation use cases with solutions and toolkits.

questions.question: Which exchange uses the GitHub API and human moderators to categorize and display related repositories?
questions.explanation: The module states that Code Exchange uses the GitHub API and human moderators.

questions.question: (Choose 3) Select all infrastructure scenarios explicitly listed for Automation Exchange use cases.
questions.explanation: The module lists Campus or Branch, Data Centre, and Service Provider scenarios.

questions.question: Which support option is described as a case-based ticket for one-on-one support?
questions.explanation: A Support Case is described as a case-based ticket used for one-on-one support.

questions.question: The Knowledge Base consists of troubleshooting articles for reference.
questions.explanation: The developer support section defines the Knowledge Base this way.

questions.question: What does SDLC describe in the module?
choices: The process of developing software from an idea through delivery
Only the coding phase of software development
questions.correctAnswer: The process of developing software from an idea through delivery
questions.explanation: SDLC is defined as the software development process from an idea to delivery.

questions.question: (Choose 6) Select all phases in the six-phase SDLC presented in the module.
questions.explanation: The module identifies these six SDLC phases.

questions.question: What document does the classic waterfall method suggest creating at the conclusion of requirements and analysis?
questions.explanation: The module says the classic waterfall method suggests creating an SRS document.

questions.question: The Design phase uses the provided SRS as a basis for designing the software.
questions.explanation: The module states that architects and developers design software based on the provided SRS.

questions.question: At the end of the Design phase, the team creates High-Level Design and _____ documents.
questions.explanation: The Design phase produces HLD and LLD documents.

questions.question: Which SDLC phase is also called the coding or development phase?
questions.explanation: The implementation phase is also called the coding or development phase.

questions.question: During which phase is software installed into the production environment?
questions.explanation: The deployment phase installs the software into the production environment.

questions.question: (Choose 4) Select all activities listed for the Maintenance phase.
questions.explanation: These four activities are listed under Maintenance.

questions.question: Which three methodologies are identified as the most popular?
questions.explanation: The module names Waterfall, Agile, and Lean as the three most popular methodologies.

questions.question: Which Agile value favors responding to change?
choices: Responding to change over following a plan
questions.correctAnswer: Responding to change over following a plan
questions.explanation: This is one of the four Agile Manifesto values shown in the module.

questions.question: (Choose 4) Select all methods listed as popular Agile methods.
questions.explanation: The module lists Scrum, Lean, XP, and FDD as popular Agile methods.

questions.question: A specific period, usually 2–4 weeks, during which a team takes on user stories is called a _____.
questions.explanation: The module defines a sprint as a specific period, usually 2–4 weeks.

questions.question: What does the backlog contain?
choices: All software features in a prioritized list
questions.correctAnswer: All software features in a prioritized list
questions.explanation: The backlog consists of all software features in a prioritized list.

questions.question: According to the module, how long should a daily stand-up meeting last at most?
questions.explanation: The scrum master should hold the daily stand-up for not more than 15 minutes.

questions.question: (Choose 4) Select all principles of Lean software development listed in the module.
questions.explanation: These are among the seven Lean principles listed in the module.

questions.question: Task switching is listed as one of the seven wastes of software development.
questions.explanation: Task switching appears in the module's list of seven wastes.

questions.question: Why does the module recommend delaying decisions when there is uncertainty?
choices: To base decisions on facts rather than opinions or speculation
questions.correctAnswer: To base decisions on facts rather than opinions or speculation
questions.explanation: The module says decisions should be delayed so they can be based on facts.

questions.question: What are software design patterns?
choices: Best-practice solutions for common software-development problems
questions.correctAnswer: Best-practice solutions for common software-development problems
questions.explanation: The module defines design patterns as best-practice solutions for common problems.

questions.question: Software design patterns are language-independent.
questions.explanation: The module explicitly states that design patterns are language-independent.

questions.question: (Choose 3) Select all three main Gang of Four pattern categories.
questions.explanation: The Gang of Four divided patterns into Creational, Structural, and Behavioral categories.

questions.question: What is a key benefit of the Observer design pattern?
choices: Observers can receive real-time data when the subject changes
It requires polling for every change
It removes the need to store observers
questions.correctAnswer: Observers can receive real-time data when the subject changes
questions.explanation: The module states that observers can get real-time data from the subject when a change occurs.

questions.question: Which MVC component is the application's data structure and manages data, logic, and rules?
questions.explanation: The Model is described as the application's data structure responsible for data, logic, and rules.

questions.question: Which MVC component acts as the middleman between the model and the view?
questions.explanation: The Controller is described as the middleman between Model and View.

questions.question: In MVC, the visual representation of the data is the _____.
questions.explanation: The View is the visual representation of the data.

questions.question: What is the purpose of version control?
choices: Manage file changes while keeping a history of those changes
Run only one file version forever
questions.correctAnswer: Manage file changes while keeping a history of those changes
questions.explanation: Version control manages changes to files and keeps their history.

questions.question: (Choose 3) Select all types of version control systems listed in the module.
questions.explanation: The module lists local, centralized, and distributed version control systems.

questions.question: Where is the repository stored in a centralized version control system?
choices: In a centralized location on a server
Only in each user's working directory
questions.correctAnswer: In a centralized location on a server
questions.explanation: CVCS stores the repository in a centralized location on a server.

questions.question: In a distributed version control system, locking is not required because individuals modify local files in their working copies.
questions.explanation: The DVCS section explicitly states that locking is not required.

questions.question: How does Git primarily store data according to the module?
questions.explanation: The module contrasts Git with systems that store differences and says Git stores snapshots.

questions.question: (Choose 3) Select all three Git stages listed in the module.
questions.explanation: Git is organized around the repository, working directory, and staging area.

questions.question: The three Git states are committed, modified, and _____.
questions.explanation: The module lists committed, modified, and staged as Git's three states.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of branching?
choices: Work independently without affecting the main code
Force one user to lock every file
questions.correctAnswer: Work independently without affecting the main code
questions.explanation: Branching enables independent work without affecting the main repository code.

questions.question: What does a pull request formalize?
choices: A request to review a contributor's changes for possible inclusion
A request to delete the .git directory
A request to authenticate a REST API
A request to create an SRS
questions.correctAnswer: A request to review a contributor's changes for possible inclusion
questions.explanation: The module describes a pull request as formalizing a request to review changes for inclusion.

questions.question: Which command creates an empty Git repository or makes an existing folder a Git repository?
questions.explanation: The module assigns this function to git init.

questions.question: Which command lists files that differ between the working directory and the parent branch?
questions.explanation: The module says git status lists files with differences in the working directory.

questions.question: Which command adds specified changes to the staging area?
questions.explanation: git add is used to add files to the staging area.

questions.question: Which command combines staged content changes into a commit and updates the local repository?
questions.explanation: The module states that git commit combines staged changes and updates the local repository.

questions.question: Which command updates a remote repository with content from the local repository?
questions.explanation: The Updating the Remote Repository section identifies git push.

questions.question: A local Git repository is automatically updated whenever another contributor updates the remote repository.
questions.explanation: The module says local copies do not update automatically; updating is a manual step.

questions.question: Which description best matches clean code in the module?
choices: Code made easy for other developers to read and understand
Code with no functions or modules
Code that cannot be unit tested
Code stored only on a remote repository
questions.correctAnswer: Code made easy for other developers to read and understand
questions.explanation: Clean code is described as code developers make easy for others to read and understand.

questions.question: (Choose 4) Select all characteristics emphasized by clean code.
questions.explanation: The module emphasizes standardization, organization, modularity, and inline comments.

questions.question: Methods and functions are blocks of code that perform tasks when executed.
questions.explanation: This is the module's definition of methods and functions.

questions.question: The three popular standard formats for exchanging information with remote APIs are XML, JSON, and _____.
questions.explanation: The module identifies XML, JSON, and YAML as the three popular formats.

questions.question: What does an API allow?
choices: One piece of software to talk to another
Only humans to access a file system
A Git branch to merge itself
A VM to become a physical host
questions.correctAnswer: One piece of software to talk to another
questions.explanation: The module defines an API as allowing one piece of software to talk to another.

questions.question: (Choose 3) Select all API use cases listed in the module.
questions.explanation: The module lists automation, data integration, and functionality integration as API use cases.

questions.question: Modern APIs can be consumed programmatically by applications and can also be used manually by humans.
questions.explanation: The module states both forms of use.

questions.question: When is a synchronous API appropriate according to the module?
choices: When requested data is readily available
Only when the client must never wait
questions.correctAnswer: When requested data is readily available
questions.explanation: The module says APIs are synchronous when data for the request is readily available.

questions.question: What must an application making a synchronous API request do before additional code execution tasks?
questions.explanation: The client must wait for the synchronous response before additional execution.

questions.question: When is an asynchronous API appropriate?
choices: When processing takes time or data is not readily available
Only when data is immediately available
questions.correctAnswer: When processing takes time or data is not readily available
questions.explanation: The module gives these conditions for asynchronous APIs.

questions.question: An asynchronous API can allow an application to continue execution without waiting for the server to finish processing the request.
questions.explanation: This is the stated performance benefit of asynchronous design.

questions.question: (Choose 3) Select all three popular API architectural styles listed in the module.
questions.explanation: The module lists RPC, SOAP, and REST.

questions.question: What model does Remote Procedure Call use?
questions.explanation: RPC is defined as a request-response model.

questions.question: What type of messaging protocol is SOAP?
questions.explanation: The module describes SOAP as an XML-based messaging protocol.

questions.question: (Choose 4) Select all elements that a SOAP message may contain.
questions.explanation: The module lists Envelope, Header, Body, and Fault.

questions.question: Which REST constraint requires the client and server to be independent?
questions.explanation: The client-server constraint states that client and server should be independent.

questions.question: Under the stateless constraint, where must information needed to make the request be supplied?
questions.explanation: The module says client requests must contain all information the server needs.

questions.question: The REST code-on-demand constraint is optional in the module.
questions.explanation: The module explicitly calls code-on-demand optional.

questions.question: A REST Web service API communicates over which protocol?
questions.explanation: The module defines a REST API as a programming interface that communicates over HTTP.

questions.question: (Choose 4) Select all four major components of a REST API request.
questions.explanation: The module lists URI, HTTP Method, Header, and Body.

questions.question: The URI component that specifies whether http or https should be used is the _____.
questions.explanation: The scheme specifies the HTTP protocol, http or https.

questions.question: Which URI component provides additional details for scope, filtering, or clarification?
questions.explanation: The Query component provides additional details for scope, filtering, or clarification.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is mapped to retrieving resource details?
questions.explanation: The module maps GET to Read/retrieve resource details.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is mapped to partial update?
questions.explanation: The module maps PATCH to Partial Update.

questions.question: (Choose 3) Select all HTTP methods that typically include a request body according to the module.
questions.explanation: The module says POST, PUT, and PATCH requests typically include a body.

questions.question: Which header key specifies the format of data in the body?
questions.explanation: Content-Type is identified as the entity header specifying body data format.

questions.question: What are the three major components of a REST API response?
questions.explanation: The module lists HTTP Status, Header, and Body.

questions.question: Which category represents client errors?
questions.explanation: The module identifies 4xx as Client Error.

questions.question: Which status code means the requested resource was created?
questions.explanation: The common status table defines 201 as Created.

questions.question: Which status code indicates valid authentication credentials are missing?
questions.explanation: The module defines 401 as lacking valid authentication credentials.

questions.question: A 503 Service Unavailable response means the server currently cannot handle the request.
questions.explanation: This is the module's description of 503.

questions.question: Breaking response data into chunks is called response _____.
questions.explanation: The module states that response pagination breaks data into chunks.

questions.question: What does authentication prove?
questions.explanation: The module states that authentication proves user identity.

questions.question: What does authorization define?
choices: User access and permission to perform an action
questions.correctAnswer: User access and permission to perform an action
questions.explanation: Authorization defines user access and permissions for requested actions.

questions.question: (Choose 3) Select all common authentication mechanisms listed in the module.
questions.explanation: The module lists Basic, Bearer, and API Key authentication.

questions.question: What does OAuth 2.0 enable a third-party application to obtain?
choices: Limited access to an HTTP service
questions.correctAnswer: Limited access to an HTTP service
questions.explanation: The module states that OAuth 2.0 enables limited access to an HTTP service.

questions.question: What is an API rate limit?
choices: A control on requests per defined unit of time
questions.correctAnswer: A control on requests per defined unit of time
questions.explanation: The module defines rate limiting in terms of request count per unit of time.

questions.question: (Choose 3) Select all purposes of rate limiting listed in the module.
choices: Provide better service and response time
correctAnswers: Provide better service and response time
questions.explanation: These three purposes are explicitly listed.

questions.question: Which algorithm queues incoming requests in arrival order and processes them at a fixed rate?
questions.explanation: The leaky bucket algorithm queues requests and processes them at a fixed rate.

questions.question: Which algorithm assigns users tokens that are removed as requests are processed?
questions.explanation: The token bucket algorithm uses a defined number of tokens and removes one per processed request.

questions.question: The rate-limit header key that indicates when the current window will reset is _____.
questions.explanation: The module identifies X-Rate Limit-Reset as the reset-time key.

questions.question: What is a webhook?
choices: An HTTP callback or POST to a specified URL when an event occurs
questions.correctAnswer: An HTTP callback or POST to a specified URL when an event occurs
questions.explanation: The module defines a webhook as an HTTP callback/POST used for event notification.

questions.question: (Choose 3) Select all requirements listed for an application consuming a webhook.
choices: Run at all times to receive POST requests
Register a URI with the webhook provider
correctAnswers: Run at all times to receive POST requests
Register a URI with the webhook provider
questions.explanation: These are the requirements listed for receiving webhook notifications.
